subject: Commercial tie-breaker: runtime parity, onboarding credits & packaging options
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@optiscale.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: michael.chen@optiscale.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring vendor replacement economics

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating a switch off our incumbent and pricing is the primary gate — specifically runtime cost parity, migration credits, and whether Redwood can match our seat-based commitments vs the incumbent's heavy consumption discounts.

Quick asks so we can brief procurement:
- A concise comparison of per-token runtime cost at our 95th percentile latency profile (P50 ~ 160ms, P95 ~ 420ms).
- A structured onramp credit proposal (one-time + staged) for a first-year commit of ~ $420k.
- Packaging options: fixed-seat bundle vs pure consumption; any hybrid you can propose.

If possible, can you share a spreadsheet we can drop into procurement's TCO model? Prefer an apples-to-apples with notes on runtime feature parity (KV cache behavior, batching constraints, prefetching).

We'd like a recommended path by end of week.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Cloud Procurement
OptiScale

---
Attachment: procurement_rundown_request.pdf (pdf - stub)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Priya Rao <priya@optiscale.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@optiscale.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring vendor replacement economics

Priya — thanks, this is helpful context. I've pulled together an initial response and an apples-to-apples workbook (attached). High level bullets up front:

- Runtime parity: For your workload profile our recommended model (RWD-XL-16) matches P50/P95 latency with equivalent KV cache semantics. We achieve similar P95 by preferring continuous batching + KV warm cache for steady streams; the attached sheet models per-token cost with and without persistent KV caching.

- Onramp credits: Proposal in the workbook is a two-part credit: a $35k immediate migration credit + staged performance credits (up to $85k) tied to go-live KPIs over the first 90 days. Total maximum one-time credits = $120k.

- Packaging: We propose a hybrid: base reserved seats (monthly committed units) to secure latency & capacity, plus a lower-cost consumption pool for burst. That preserves unit economics while giving you operational headroom. The workbook lays out 3 scenarios: Seat-first, Consumption-first, and Hybrid.

I've looped in Jonas (sales lead) for commercial details and Marissa for onboarding/implementation risk.

Next steps: Jonas can walk through the workbook tomorrow (Wed) 10am PT if that works. If procurement wants a formalized term sheet after that we can prepare it and include the SOW stub.

Attached: Redwood_OptiScale_Swap_Pricing_20280821.xlsx (xlsx - stub), SOW_OptiScale_Onramp_draft.pdf (pdf - stub)

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Priya Rao <priya@optiscale.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, michael.chen@optiscale.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring vendor replacement economics

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications from our side to make the sheet procurement-ready before the call:

1) Measured unit costs: In the workbook we show three unit-cost columns: raw token execution, execution + KV effectiveness (assumes 35% token savings from persistent caching), and blended after batching. Which column does procurement want to use in their template?

2) Credits timing: The staged performance credits are released based on three milestones: onboard completion, latency SLA acceptance, and a 30-day throughput smoke test. We can accelerate one milestone if you can commit to a pilot acceptance window (10 business days).

3) Packaging nuance: Seat-based commitments lock-in latency SLO & capacity reservations (good for predictable latency-sensitive calls). The consumption pool has a lower nominal unit cost but no latency guarantees. We recommend hybrid if you expect bursty traffic with some latency-sensitive segments.

Ask: Priya/Michael, can you confirm anticipated steady-state split (% of calls latency-sensitive) so we can mark the right scenario in the workbook? If not available tomorrow we can model 60/40 and show sensitivity.

Also flagged a technical footnote in the workbook about egress and KV snapshot sizing that typically drives last-mile differences in onboarding effort — Marissa, can you validate the estimate?

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya@optiscale.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@optiscale.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring vendor replacement economics

Jonas — thanks, this all looks good. We ran a quick usage slice and the latency-sensitive subset is roughly 52% of total calls during peak (35% steady-state). Please model 52/48 for peak-plan costs and include a sensitivity at 40/60.

Procurement wants the sheet and a short one-page term summary prior to the internal vendor selection meeting on Friday. Can you share both by EOD today? If you can also call out any non-recurring engineering effort (NRE) hours and a not-to-exceed estimate, that will speed approvals.

We'll be on the 10am PT slot for the walkthrough.

Best,
Priya
